newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasolines drop despite refinery fire.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasolines drop despite refinery fire.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale gasoline prices fell late Monday after a sharp decline in energy futures overshadowed a morning fire at Texaco's Los Angeles-area refinery.
The blaze, which shut the plant's 9,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) alkylation unit, began at 1215 a.m. Pacific time (1515 EST/1015 GMT) and still burned late Monday.
An early 2.75 cent rally in CARB Los Angeles gasoline prices faded late, with January supplies ending 1.25 cents a gallon below Friday's market. Final assessments put CARB at 76/77 cents a gallon.
The downturn came on the heels of milder forecasts for the Northeastern U.S., which pulled down NYMEX.
February heating oil settled off 2.45 cents a gallon to 69.70 cents while crude slipped 90 cents.
"This is the third day we're down on the (New York Mercantile Exchange) and is it a trend?" a trader asked.
"That's what's making (sellers) come out of the woodwork," he said.
West Coast spot distillate prices generally ended the day one cent below Friday, under pressure from NYMEX.
